fundamental_action_reconstruction/STRICT_EQUATION_SHEET_KERNEL_TO_LTOTAL_CURRENT.md:1781:## P2521/S1471 single nonzero node-anchor equivalence certificate

fundamental_action_reconstruction/STRICT_EQUATION_SHEET_KERNEL_TO_LTOTAL_CURRENT.md:1783:`P2521/S1471` refines the P2520 endpoint-subkey lattice by separating endpoint sufficiency from endpoint uniqueness.  Once the left beta-normalization anchor `y(0)=0` is admitted, any one nonzero strict node anchor `y(log d*)=(4/5)log d*` with `d*>1` pins the affine kernel, because the determinant of `[[1,0],[1,log d*]]` is `log d*>0`.  The finite audit checks every `d*=2..11`: each node reconstructs `delta=4/5`, `eta=9/5`, and all strict nodes `d=1..11` with zero residual within arithmetic tolerance.
fundamental_action_reconstruction/STRICT_EQUATION_SHEET_KERNEL_TO_LTOTAL_CURRENT.md:1787:## P2522/S1472 two-node anchor basis equivalence certificate

fundamental_action_reconstruction/STRICT_EQUATION_SHEET_KERNEL_TO_LTOTAL_CURRENT.md:1789:`P2522/S1472` continues P2521 by showing that the left-normalization-plus-one-node basis is itself not unique.  For the affine running exponent `y=b+a ell`, any two distinct strict node anchors `y(log d_i)=(4/5)log d_i` and `y(log d_j)=(4/5)log d_j` have determinant `log(d_j/d_i) != 0` and solve `b=0`, `a=4/5`, hence `beta=1`, `eta=9/5`.  The finite audit checks all 55 distinct node pairs in `d=1..11`: every pair derives the left normalization, pins the same slope, and reconstructs all audited strict nodes with zero residual within arithmetic tolerance.
fundamental_action_reconstruction/STRICT_EQUATION_SHEET_KERNEL_TO_LTOTAL_CURRENT.md:1793:## P2523/S1473 pairwise secant consistency certificate

fundamental_action_reconstruction/STRICT_EQUATION_SHEET_KERNEL_TO_LTOTAL_CURRENT.md:1795:`P2523/S1473` turns the P2522 node-pair basis equivalence into a basis-independent finite consistency audit.  For the strict target node data `y_d=(4/5)log d` on `d=1..11`, all 55 pairwise secants have slope `4/5`, all 165 triangle additive `y`-cocycles vanish, and the affine projection on columns `[1, log(d)]` recovers intercept `0`, slope `4/5`, hence `beta=1`, `eta=9/5`, with zero residual within arithmetic tolerance.
